2010_003_031610regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Regular Meeting of Tuesday, March 16, 2010, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It carries the March 2 and March 9 minutes, the January and February 2010 Treasurer's Reports with their Pentamation check registers, ACH and wire transfer listings, four bid awards, curriculum reports on elementary reading and middle school health, first readings of six board policies plus new Policy D-1106 Fixed Assets, and a closed session on TESPA negotiations. The March 2 minutes record Resolution 10-025, authorizing administration to implement approximately $6 million in budget adjustments and draw on fund equity for the projected 2010-2011 deficit.

## Meeting

Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday, March 16, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Recognition items honored the district's Outstanding Teachers and Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union mini-grant recipients, introduced by community relations director Tim McAvoy and MSGCU's Sally Gibson.

## Consent agenda and prior minutes

Item 5 covered the March 2, 2010 meeting minutes, the March 9, 2010 workshop minutes, the January and February 2010 Treasurer's Reports, and item 5.D, added by resolution. The March 2 minutes (all seven members present; adjourned 9:12 p.m.) record Resolution 10-018 recognizing Sen. John Pappageorge and Rep. Marty Knollenberg over the October 19, 2009 line-item veto of 20j funding, described as cutting Troy by nearly $3 million annually, or $248.18 per pupil, alongside 40 other Michigan communities. Bid awards from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund followed: artificial turf replacement to General Sports Venue, $711,137.00 (10-020); tennis court updates to Best Asphalt, $228,690.00 (10-021); SMART Interactive White Boards to Smart Ed. Services, $418,964.50 (10-022). Resolution 10-023 approved a Sodexo Management, Inc. contract addendum; 10-024 endorsed the Legislative Commission on Statutory Mandates reports; 10-025 authorized approximately $6 million in budget adjustments plus a draw on fund equity for 2010-2011.

## Curriculum

Item 7.A reports on the elementary reading program, under revision since the 2006/07 school year and presented by Dr. Karen Reese (Morse) and Trudi Motzenbecker (Wattles): a Reading Workshop approach, Making Meaning read-alouds, and Fountas and Pinnell as the common kindergarten-through-fifth-grade assessment. Item 7.B recommends Teen Health, Course 3 (Bronson, Cleary, Hubbard; Glencoe, copyright 2009) beginning 2010-2011 in place of a text copyrighted 2001, its human sexuality and HIV/AIDS chapters having been approved by the Sex Education Advisory Board on November 9, 2009. Item 7.C adopts Literature, published by McDougal Littell, for grades six through 12, phased in over two years - an estimated $469,369 from 2010-2011 secondary textbook budgets for the high school program and $321,052 from 2011-2012 budgets for middle school.

## Policies and closed session

Item 9.A is a first reading of B-1208 Voting, B-1211 Public Participation in Board of Education Meetings, B-1301 Agenda Format for Regular Meetings, C-1402 Smoking, new D-1106 Fixed Assets (items over $5,000 with useful life exceeding one year), K-1303 and K-1304, all pending adoption April 20, 2010. The meeting closes with a resolution to enter closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to discuss TESPA negotiations.

## Meeting and agenda

Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday, March 16, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district address 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us); meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Agenda: Pledge; Recognition of Outstanding Teachers and of Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union mini-grant recipients, opened by community relations director Tim McAvoy with MSGCU's Sally Gibson presenting; item 3.A adding item 5.D; Public Communication; consent agenda 5.A-5.D; curriculum items 7.A-7.C; business items 8.A-8.C; 9.A board policy first readings; adjournment; and a closed session on TESPA negotiations. Superintendent of Schools is Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.

## Minutes of March 2, 2010

Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Underwood, with all seven members present - Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo - plus Superintendent Fowler, eleven administrators and about 70 audience members; adjourned 9:12 p.m.; signed by Secretary Nancy L. Philippart. Resolution 10-018 (Yes 7, No 0) recognized State Sen. John Pappageorge and State Rep. Marty Knollenberg for work to restore 20j funding after Governor Granholm signed a school aid bill on October 19, 2009 containing a line-item veto of 20j funds, which the resolution says cut funding to Troy students by nearly $3 million annually, or $248.18 per pupil, hit 40 other Michigan communities, and broke the promise made to Troy voters as part of Proposal A in 1994. Resolution 10-019 approved the consent agenda. Resolutions 10-020 through 10-022 awarded, all from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, artificial turf replacement to General Sports Venue at $711,137.00, tennis court updates to Best Asphalt at $228,690.00, and SMART Interactive White Boards to Smart Ed. Services at $418,964.50. Resolution 10-023 approved a Sodexo Management, Inc. contract addendum assigning Gayle Moran as General Manager effective January 18, 2010. Resolution 10-024 endorsed the Legislative Commission on Statutory Mandates - created by P.A. 98 of 2007 as amended by P.A. 356 of 2008 - and its June 2009 interim and December 2009 final reports on the Headlee Amendment, Article IX, Section 29. Resolution 10-025, after a report by Mr. Adamczyk, authorized administration to implement approximately $6 million in budget adjustments and draw on existing fund equity for the projected 2010-2011 deficit. Bruce Bloomingdale spoke on the budget process; student representatives Enxhi Xhafa (Athens) and Andrew Michail (Troy High) reported. The March 9 workshop minutes (6:10 p.m. to 10:05 p.m.) list personal curriculum, graduation requirements, the seven policies below, and 1000-Day Plan status; staff left at 8:50 p.m. before discussion of the superintendent's evaluation.

## Item 5.D - anti-virus software licenses

Invitations went to 6 bidders with 3 responding; reviewed with Scott Bryan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, 248-823-5090). The bid, issued March 1, 2010 for five years of Trend Micro licensing and opened March 15, drew two identical bids of $119,273.85 for the five-year term; each low bidder offered a 10% discount for outright purchase, yielding $107,346.47. Networks Group, Inc. was recommended on the basis of Michigan headquarters and reference checks. Networks Group and CDW Government LLC bid identical pricing (base five-year $119,273.85, alternate $155,025.00); Dell Marketing bid a base five-year total of $288,205.50. The NetWorks Group quote (TSD-31610-TMS-60M, by Paul Alexander, Ann Arbor) shows a discount of $11,927.38 and a total of $107,346.47, valid through March 31, 2010. The award is an expenditure of the 2009-2010 through 2013-2014 General Funds.

## Curriculum items 7.A, 7.B, 7.C

7.A: the elementary reading program has been under review since the 2006/07 school year, with a committee co-chaired by principals Janice Brzezinski (Hill) and Lois Byrne (Martell) and teachers Dr. Karen Reese (Morse) and Trudi Motzenbecker (Wattles), who present. Decisions include Reading Workshop as the instructional approach, Making Meaning read-alouds, Fountas and Pinnell as the common kindergarten-through-fifth-grade assessment, and units of study revised 1/18/10; cited research includes Richard Allington's six Ts, Lucy Calkins, and Keene and Zimmerman. Reader Profile drafts dated 8/18/09 cover Grade One (levels D/4-E/7, 18-30 high-frequency words, at least 98% accuracy) and Grade Five (level U/50, Dolch first 1000); revision is planned for summer 2010. 7.B: middle school health teachers reviewed materials in fall 2009, and human sexuality, HIV and AIDS content was approved by the Sex Education Advisory Board on November 9, 2009; Alicia Wahls (Smith Middle School) and Larry Hahn (Baker Middle School principal) present. The committee unanimously recommends Teen Health, Course 3 by Bronson, Cleary and Hubbard (Glencoe, copyright 2009) for 2010-2011, replacing a text copyrighted 2001; Decision for Health (Holt McDougal, 2008) and Health and Wellness (MacMillan, 2009) were also reviewed. 7.C: a resolution adopts Literature, published by McDougal Littell, for grades six through 12, phased in over two years - high school beginning 2010-2011 at an estimated $469,369 from 2010-2011 secondary textbook budgets, middle school beginning 2011-2012 at an estimated $321,052 from 2011-2012 budgets.

## Business items 8.A, 8.B, 8.C

8.A, Athens High School media center furniture (Bid #9648, opened January 12, 2010; 16 invited, 8 responding; reviewed by Dr. Rich Machesky, principal Lara Dixon, district carpenter Gary Bell, Michael Adamczyk and purchasing supervisor Frank E. Lams, Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083): the award splits between Office Express at $16,957.18 (media seating $13,374.93, miscellaneous seating $3,582.25) and 3rd Coast at $66,703.75 (shelving, tables, custom counter), total $83,660.93 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, with lounge furniture deferred to the April 20th meeting. 8.B, media center carpet (Bid #9658, opened February 23, 2010; 14 invited, 4 responding; reviewed with operations director Ken Miller): Conventional Carpet at $27,040.00 (removal $2,370.00, installation $24,670.00), ahead of Cohn's Commercial Floor Covering $29,993.25, Floorcraft $30,700.00 and Imperial Floor Covering $34,160.00. 8.C, bus security cameras (Bid #9661, opened February 24, 2010; 12 invited, 5 responding; reviewed with transportation supervisor Dominick Asaro and First Student contract manager Amy Johnson): Unity School Bus Parts at $49,895.00 for a Seon system - 20 complete systems at $29,600.00 and 41 decoy systems at $20,295.00 - within a budgetary constraint of $50,000.00, so that the twenty cameras plus the existing five can be moved among all non-spare buses.

## Item 9.A - board policies, and closed session

First readings, all pending adoption April 20, 2010: B-1208 Voting (adopted January 16, 1979); B-1211 Public Participation in Board of Education Meetings (revised April 1988, March 17, 1998, July 10, 2007, March 17, 2009), whose revision limits participation to 60 minutes per meeting - about 30 minutes at the beginning for agenda items and 30 at the end for non-agenda items - requires a Speaker Request Form filed with the Secretary, and allows recognized speakers up to three minutes; B-1301 Agenda Format for Regular Meetings (revised September 28, 1988, October 3, 1989, March 17, 1998, June 19, 2007); C-1402 Smoking (adopted February 2, 1999, revised September 2003), following Public Act 140 of 1993, with smoking also prohibited at athletic fields and tobacco use banned 24 hours a day, seven days a week; new D-1106 Fixed Assets, tracking items costing more than $5,000 with useful life exceeding one year plus theft-prone items under $5,000, classified as land, buildings, improvements other than buildings, construction in progress, and machinery and equipment; K-1303 Political and/or Commercial Advertising by District Employees (adopted May 3, 1976, revised January 16, 1979 and April 21, 1998); and K-1304 Advertising on School District Property and in School District Electronic Media (adopted April 19, 1976, revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, April 15, 2003), which treats district property and media as a nonpublic forum and lists 16 prohibited categories. The packet closes with a resolution, by roll call of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo, to enter closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to discuss TESPA negotiations.
